1	# PROGRAM.md — the live research program
2	
3	This is the single state document of the continuous research loop.
4	Every cycle reads it first and updates it last. Keep it honest, keep
5	it current, keep it short — history goes to `archive/`, results go to
6	`experiments/` and `novel/`.
7	
8	## Goal
9	
10	An O(polylog) algorithm computing the n-th prime p(n) (equivalently
11	π(x)) exactly. Target: p(10^100) in < 1 s, 100% accurate.
12	
13	**Honest position:** every known computation route is blocked — 730+
14	approaches catalogued in `status/CLOSED_PATHS.md`, four obstruction
15	theorems, the information-theoretic barrier (~√x zeta-zero phases,
16	GUE-random, behind the last ~50% of digits). The goal may require
17	mathematics that does not exist. The deliverable of each cycle is
18	honest progress: working algorithms/protocols, new structural facts
19	with measurements, precisely-closed questions with mechanisms,
20	adjacent-problem wins. Never a faked breakthrough.
21

# PROGRAM.md — the live research program

This is the single state document of the continuous research loop.
Every cycle reads it first and updates it last. Keep it honest, keep
it current, keep it short — history goes to `archive/`, results go to
`experiments/` and `novel/`.

## Goal

An O(polylog) algorithm computing the n-th prime p(n) (equivalently
π(x)) exactly. Target: p(10^100) in < 1 s, 100% accurate.

**Honest position:** every known computation route is blocked — 730+
approaches catalogued in `status/CLOSED_PATHS.md`, four obstruction
theorems, the information-theoretic barrier (~√x zeta-zero phases,
GUE-random, behind the last ~50% of digits). The goal may require
mathematics that does not exist. The deliverable of each cycle is
honest progress: working algorithms/protocols, new structural facts
with measurements, precisely-closed questions with mechanisms,
adjacent-problem wins. Never a faked breakthrough.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""
3	pcs_commit.py -- S508, a hash-based multilinear polynomial commitment (tensor /
4	Ligero-Brakedown style) with a SUB-sqrt(x) verifier, for the chain's two
5	one-time S_0 base closes.
6	
7	WHERE THIS SITS.  The compressed pi(x) chain (compressed_layer.run_chain) is now
8	per-layer LEAF-EVAL-FREE (S506 batch_ub): every per-layer carried claim threads
9	to the base, and the only verifier work whose cost grows with x is ONE-TIME --
10	the two S_0 base closes, each a DIRECT mle_eval over an O(sqrt x)=2^nb-size table
11	(`C == mle_eval(S0, z)` at compressed_layer.py:1047).  The whole-chain verifier
12	op-count (S507 `--bench-verifier-ops`) is therefore Theta(sqrt x): per-layer 0,
13	one-time 2*2^nb.  That one-time 2^nb term is the LAST thing between the current
14	state and a SUCCINCT (polylog / sub-sqrt x) verifier.
15	
16	WHAT THIS BUILDS.  A polynomial commitment for a multilinear S~ over nb variables
17	whose EVALUATION-PROOF VERIFIER is O(sqrt(2^nb) * polylog) = O(x^{1/4} * polylog),
18	i.e. sub-sqrt(x).  Tensor / Ligero-Brakedown construction:
19	
20	  * Reshape the 2^nb-entry table S (MSB-first) into an r x k matrix M, r=2^{n1},
21	    k=2^{n2}, n1+n2=nb (row bits = high n1, col bits = low n2: M = S.reshape(r,k)).
22	  * eq~(pt, .) factors over the bit split, eq~(pt,w)=eq~(pt_hi,w_hi)*eq~(pt_lo,w_lo),
23	    so with the tensor vectors a=eq_table(pt_hi) (len r), b=eq_table(pt_lo) (len k):
24	        S~(pt) = sum_{i,j} M[i,j] a[i] b[j] = a^T M b.
25	  * COMMIT: Reed-Solomon-encode each ROW of M (a degree-<k message) to a length-N
26	    codeword (N=blowup*k evaluation points), giving Mhat (r x N); Merkle-commit the
27	    N COLUMNS of Mhat (sha256, the collision-resistant-hash / random-oracle
28	    stand-in).  The commitment is the Merkle root.
29	  * OPEN (Fiat-Shamir, non-interactive): derive a proximity vector rho<-RO(root,pt,
30	    claimed) (len r); the prover sends the two combined MESSAGES v=a^T M (the
31	    evaluation combination, len k) and w=rho^T M (the proximity combination, len k),
32	    then opens t columns Q<-RO(root,pt,claimed,v,w) with Merkle paths.
33	  * VERIFY:  (1) evaluation binding  <v, b> == claimed;  (2) for each queried col c:
34	    the revealed column Mhat[:,c] hashes to the committed root (Merkle), AND
35	    Enc(v)[c] == <a, Mhat[:,c]>  AND  Enc(w)[c] == <rho, Mhat[:,c]>  (encoding is
36	    linear, so for an honest codeword matrix Enc(a^T M)[c] = a^T Mhat[:,c]).
37	
38	  Verifier cost: reading v,w O(k); <v,b> O(k); per queried column two length-r dot
39	  products + two length-k encodings = O(t(r+k)) field ops + O(t r) hashed elements
40	  for the Merkle paths.  With r,k ~ 2^{nb/2} ~ x^{1/4} and t fixed, that is
41	  O(x^{1/4} * polylog) -- SUB-sqrt(x).  The full 2^nb table never touches the
42	  verifier; it lives only in the prover's commit/open.
43	
44	SOUNDNESS (standard Ligero/Brakedown, under a collision-resistant hash / RO).
45	The Merkle root binds Mhat (collision resistance).  The random proximity test
46	(rho, t columns) forces the committed Mhat to be close to a matrix whose rows are
47	codewords, so it decodes to a unique M.  The evaluation columns then pin v=a^T M,
48	and <v,b>=claimed forces claimed = S~(pt) for that committed M.  A wrong claimed
49	value fails (1) outright (the honest v has <v,b>=true value); a prover who instead
50	forges v' with <v',b>=wrong has Enc(v') differing from a^T Mhat in >= N-(k-1)
51	columns (two degree-<k polys agree on < k points), caught by some queried column
52	with prob >= 1-((k-1)/N)^t; a tampered (non-codeword) committed row is caught by
53	the proximity column checks with the same bound; a tampered REVEALED column fails
54	its Merkle path.  This is a soundness ARGUMENT verified here empirically by the
55	cheating-prover tests, not a machine-checked proof.
56	
57	HONEST SCOPE.  (i) The win is in the SCALING (op count slope ~0.25 in x, sub-sqrt),
58	NOT the absolute count at reachable n: the verifier touches ~ t*(2r+2k) ~ 4t*x^{1/4}
59	field elements, which only drops below the direct 2^nb close once 2^{nb/2} > ~4t,
60	i.e. nb > ~2*log2(4t) (~nb>=15, n>=30 at t=32) -- beyond the demo's reachable n,
61	exactly like the S506 wall-clock note.  The bench reports the slope to show
62	sub-sqrt scaling regardless of the crossover constant.  (ii) This trades
63	UNCONDITIONALITY for full succinctness: soundness now rests on the hash (RO/CRH),
64	whereas the rest of the chain verifier is unconditional and Õ(sqrt x).  (iii) RS
65	needs N <= q distinct points; fine at demo n, and a production system swaps in a
66	field-size-free linear code (Brakedown's expander code) behind the SAME
67	commit/open/verify interface -- the tensor reduction and the cost are unchanged.
68	
69	WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS.  verify disagreeing with mle_eval on an honest opening;
70	a forged opening / wrong claimed value / tampered codeword row accepted (above the
71	field bound); the verifier op count not sub-sqrt-x (slope -> 0.5 not -> 0.25); or
72	threading it into run_chain(--commit-base) changing the chain verdict / claimed pi.
73	
74	Usage:
75	  python3 pcs_commit.py --selftest
76	  python3 pcs_commit.py --bench
77	  python3 pcs_commit.py --bench --field big
78	"""
79	
80	import argparse
81	import hashlib
82	import time
83	
84	import numpy as np
85	
86	from compressed_prover_mult_trace import (DEFAULT_Q as Q, BIG_Q, SMALL_Q,
87	                                          FIELDS, eq_table, mle_eval)
88	
89	
90	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
91	# hashing / Merkle  (sha256 = the collision-resistant-hash / random-oracle stand-in)
92	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
93	
94	def _digest(*parts):
95	    h = hashlib.sha256()
96	    for p in parts:
97	        h.update(p)
98	    return h.digest()
99	
100	
101	def _wid(q):
102	    """Fixed byte width to serialize a field element of F_q unambiguously."""
103	    return (int(q).bit_length() + 7) // 8 + 1
104	
105	
106	def _ser(vec, q):
107	    """Deterministic byte serialization of a field vector (for hashing/FS)."""
108	    w = _wid(q)
109	    return b"".join(int(int(x) % q).to_bytes(w, "big") for x in vec)
110	
111	
112	def _challenges(seed, label, n, mod):
113	    """n field/index challenges in [0, mod) from RO(seed || label || ctr)."""
114	    out = []
115	    i = 0
116	    while len(out) < n:
117	        d = _digest(seed, label, i.to_bytes(4, "big"))
118	        out.append(int.from_bytes(d, "big") % mod)
119	        i += 1
120	    return out
121	
122	
123	def _distinct_challenges(seed, label, n, mod):
124	    """Up to n DISTINCT indices in [0, mod) (column queries)."""
125	    seen, out, i = set(), [], 0
126	    while len(out) < n and len(seen) < mod:
127	        c = int.from_bytes(_digest(seed, label, i.to_bytes(4, "big")), "big") % mod
128	        i += 1
129	        if c not in seen:
130	            seen.add(c)
131	            out.append(c)
132	    return out
133	
134	
135	def _merkle_build(leaves):
136	    """Binary Merkle tree over leaf digests (padded to a power of two with a
137	    fixed pad leaf).  Returns the level list (levels[0]=leaves, levels[-1]=[root])."""
138	    n = len(leaves)
139	    m = 1
140	    while m < n:
141	        m <<= 1
142	    pad = _digest(b"pad")
143	    level = list(leaves) + [pad] * (m - n)
144	    levels = [level]
145	    while len(level) > 1:
146	        level = [_digest(level[2 * i], level[2 * i + 1])
147	                 for i in range(len(level) // 2)]
148	        levels.append(level)
149	    return levels
150	
151	
152	def _merkle_path(levels, idx):
153	    path = []
154	    for lvl in levels[:-1]:
155	        path.append(lvl[idx ^ 1])
156	        idx >>= 1
157	    return path
158	
159	
160	def _merkle_check(root, idx, leaf, path):
161	    h = leaf
162	    for sib in path:
163	        h = _digest(h, sib) if (idx & 1) == 0 else _digest(sib, h)
164	        idx >>= 1
165	    return h == root
166	
167	
168	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
169	# Reed-Solomon encoding (the linear code; coefficient form, points 0..N-1)
170	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
171	
172	def _enc_point(coeffs, x, q):
173	    """Evaluate sum_j coeffs[j] x^j at field point x (Horner).  This is Enc(.)[c]
174	    for evaluation point x = c, the verifier's per-column encoding (O(k))."""
175	    acc = 0
176	    for cj in reversed(coeffs):
177	        acc = (acc * x + int(cj)) % q
178	    return acc
179	
180	
181	def _encode_rows(M, Ncode, q):
182	    """Mhat[i][c] = Enc(M[i])[c], the RS codeword of every row at points 0..Ncode-1."""
183	    return [[_enc_point(row, c, q) for c in range(Ncode)] for row in M]
184	
185	
186	def _leaves_from_Mhat(Mhat, r, Ncode, q):
187	    return [_digest(b"col", c.to_bytes(4, "big"),
188	                    _ser([Mhat[i][c] for i in range(r)], q))
189	            for c in range(Ncode)]
190	
191	
192	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
193	# Brakedown-style linear-time EXPANDER code (the field-size-free row code)
194	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
195	#
196	# WHY.  The RS row code (above) needs N = blowup*k <= q distinct evaluation
197	# points -- a demo constraint that caps the committable table size and forced
198	# the large runs onto the 61-bit BIG_Q.  Brakedown's recursive expander code is
199	# a LINEAR, LINEAR-TIME-ENCODABLE code with constant relative distance over ANY
200	# field -- no distinct-point / N<=q requirement.  It plugs in behind the SAME
201	# commit/prove/verify interface: only (i) how a row is encoded (commit) and (ii)
202	# how the combined messages v,w are re-encoded (verify) change.  The tensor
203	# reduction S~(pt)=a^T M b and the homomorphic column check
204	#     <a, Mhat[:,c]> = sum_i a[i] Enc(M[i])[c] = Enc(a^T M)[c] = Enc(v)[c]
205	# hold for ANY linear Enc, so the soundness argument and the O(t(r+k))=O(x^{1/4})
206	# verifier are unchanged; only the code (and its relative distance delta) differ.
207	#
208	# CONSTRUCTION (Spielman / Druk-Ishai recursive code, as instantiated in
209	# Brakedown, Golovnev-Lee-Setty-Thaler-Wahby 2021).  Systematic, recursive:
210	#     Enc_n(x) = x  ||  Enc_{nm}(A x)  ||  B (Enc_{nm}(A x)),   nm = ceil(n/2)
211	# where A (nm x n) and B (pn x ne) are SPARSE matrices over F_q and the base case
212	# (n <= BASE) is a dense systematic code x || R x.  A and B are COLUMN-REGULAR
213	# (every input coordinate is assigned to `coldeg` output rows) so EVERY input
214	# influences the parity -- this is what kills the weight-1 codewords a plain
215	# low-density generator matrix (LDGM) would have, and is the measured difference
216	# between rel-distance ~0.003 (row-regular, columns missed) and ~0.45 (here).
217	# Encode is LINEAR-TIME: each level costs O(coldeg*n) field mults and the message
218	# lengths shrink geometrically (sum = O(coldeg*n) = O(k) = O(x^{1/4})).
219	#
220	# The matrices are derived deterministically from a FIXED public seed + the size
221	# n only (column indices) and reduced mod q (values), so the prover's commit and
222	# the verifier's re-encode build the IDENTICAL linear map -- a fixed public code.
223	#
224	# HONEST SCOPE.  The relative distance delta is the security parameter: the
225	# consistency / proximity tests catch a cheating prover with prob >= 1-(1-delta)^t.
226	# We MEASURE delta on the demo instances (selftest asserts min low-weight-codeword
227	# relative weight >= 0.3; it runs ~0.42-0.65) and pick t accordingly.  Brakedown's
228	# *analyzed* parameters give a proven delta (~0.07) with t~148 for 100-bit
229	# security; the construction shape here is theirs, the constants are demo-scale and
230	# distance-measured rather than from the asymptotic expander bound.
231	
232	_EXP_SEED = b"pcs-expander-v1"        # fixed public seed for the code's matrices
233	_EXP_BASE = 4                         # base-case message-length threshold
234	_EXP_COLDEG = 4                       # column degree of the sparse matrices A, B
235	_EXP_PLAN_CACHE = {}                  # (n, q) -> plan; matrices are deterministic
236	
237	
238	def _exp_val(label, i, j, q):
239	    """A NONZERO field element from RO(seed||label||i||j) (matrix entry)."""
240	    v = int.from_bytes(_digest(_EXP_SEED, label, i.to_bytes(4, "big"),
241	                               j.to_bytes(4, "big")), "big") % q
242	    return v if v != 0 else 1
243	
244	
245	def _exp_sparse_colreg(nr, nc, coldeg, q, tag):
246	    """A COLUMN-REGULAR sparse matrix (nr x nc): every column is placed in
247	    `coldeg` distinct rows with nonzero values.  Returned as row lists of
248	    (col, val) -- every input coordinate thus reaches >= coldeg output rows."""
249	    rows = [[] for _ in range(nr)]
250	    d = min(coldeg, nr)
251	    for c in range(nc):
252	        rs = _distinct_challenges(_EXP_SEED, tag + b":r" + c.to_bytes(4, "big"),
253	                                  d, nr)
254	        for j, ri in enumerate(rs):
255	            rows[ri].append((c, _exp_val(tag + b":v", ri, c * 97 + j, q)))
256	    return rows
257	
258	
259	def _exp_dense(nr, nc, q, tag):
260	    """A dense matrix (nr x nc) as row lists of (col, val) -- the base parity."""
261	    return [[(c, _exp_val(tag + b":v", i, c, q)) for c in range(nc)]
262	            for i in range(nr)]
263	
264	
265	def _exp_plan(n, q):
266	    """Recursive code plan for message length n over F_q.  A plan is either
267	    ('base', n, N, R) or ('rec', n, N, A, sub_plan, B); N is the codeword length.
268	    Deterministic in (n, q); cached."""
269	    key = (n, q)
270	    if key in _EXP_PLAN_CACHE:
271	        return _EXP_PLAN_CACHE[key]
272	    if n <= _EXP_BASE:
273	        pn = n                                   # base parity length (rate 1/2)
274	        R = _exp_dense(pn, n, q, b"baseR%d" % n)
275	        plan = ("base", n, n + pn, R)
276	    else:
277	        nm = -(-n // 2)                          # ceil(n/2)
278	        A = _exp_sparse_colreg(nm, n, _EXP_COLDEG, q, b"A%d" % n)
279	        sub = _exp_plan(nm, q)
280	        ne = sub[2]

282	        B = _exp_sparse_colreg(pn, ne, _EXP_COLDEG, q, b"B%d" % n)
283	        plan = ("rec", n, n + ne + pn, A, sub, B)

288	def _exp_matvec(rows, x, q, ops=None):
289	    """Sparse/dense mat-vec over F_q; rows are (col, val) lists.  Counts field
290	    multiplies into ops[0] if given (the linear-time encode op count)."""
291	    out = []
292	    cnt = 0
293	    for row in rows:
294	        acc = 0
295	        for (c, v) in row:
296	            acc += v * x[c]
297	            cnt += 1
298	        out.append(acc % q)
299	    if ops is not None:
300	        ops[0] += cnt
301	    return out

304	def _exp_encode(msg, q, plan=None, ops=None):
305	    """Encode a length-n message to its length-N codeword (systematic, linear).
306	    O(coldeg*n) = O(n) field mults; counted into ops[0] if given."""
307	    n = len(msg)
308	    if plan is None:
309	        plan = _exp_plan(n, q)
310	    if plan[0] == "base":
311	        _, _, _, R = plan
312	        return [int(m) % q for m in msg] + _exp_matvec(R, msg, q, ops)
313	    _, _, _, A, sub, B = plan
314	    y = _exp_matvec(A, msg, q, ops)
315	    ye = _exp_encode(y, q, sub, ops)
316	    z = _exp_matvec(B, ye, q, ops)
317	    return [int(m) % q for m in msg] + ye + z

320	def _exp_min_basis_rel_weight(k, q):
321	    """min over basis vectors e_j of  weight(Enc(e_j)) / N  -- the quantity that
322	    governs the forge cheat (the forged-v difference is delta*Enc(e_{j0})).  A
323	    MEASURED lower bound on the code's relative distance for the soundness claim."""
324	    pl = _exp_plan(k, q)
325	    N = pl[2]
326	    wmin = N
327	    for j in range(k):
328	        e = [0] * k
329	        e[j] = 1
330	        cw = _exp_encode(e, q, pl)
331	        wmin = min(wmin, sum(1 for v in cw if v % q != 0))
332	    return wmin / N

335	def _code_ncode(code, k, q, blowup):
336	    """Codeword length N for the chosen row code (independent verifier recompute)."""
337	    if code == "rs":
338	        return max(blowup * k, k + 1)
339	    if code == "expander":
340	        return _exp_plan(k, q)[2]
341	    raise ValueError("unknown code %r" % (code,))

348	def commit(S, q=Q, blowup=4, code="rs"):
349	    """Commit to the multilinear S~ given its 2^nb-value table S (MSB-first).
350	    Returns a commitment dict; the PUBLIC commitment is `com["root"]`, the rest
351	    is prover state used by prove().  Prover cost O(r*k*N)=O(x^{3/4}) (one-time,
352	    within the prover's Õ(x) budget).  `code` selects the linear row code:
353	    "rs" (Reed-Solomon, needs N<=q) or "expander" (Brakedown-style, field-size-
354	    free)."""
355	    S = [int(x) % q for x in np.asarray(S).ravel().tolist()]
356	    N0 = len(S)
357	    nb = N0.bit_length() - 1
358	    assert (1 << nb) == N0, "table size must be a power of two"
359	    n2 = nb // 2
360	    n1 = nb - n2
361	    r, k = 1 << n1, 1 << n2
362	    M = [[S[i * k + j] for j in range(k)] for i in range(r)]
363	    if code == "rs":
364	        Ncode = max(blowup * k, k + 1)      # distance N-k+1 >= 2
365	        assert Ncode <= q, "RS needs Ncode <= q distinct points (raise q for large nb)"
366	        Mhat = _encode_rows(M, Ncode, q)
367	    elif code == "expander":
368	        pl = _exp_plan(k, q)                # field-size-free; no N<=q requirement
369	        Ncode = pl[2]
370	        Mhat = [_exp_encode(row, q, pl) for row in M]
371	    else:
372	        raise ValueError("unknown code %r" % (code,))
373	    levels = _merkle_build(_leaves_from_Mhat(Mhat, r, Ncode, q))
374	    return dict(root=levels[-1][0], M=M, Mhat=Mhat, levels=levels,
375	                r=r, k=k, n1=n1, n2=n2, nb=nb, Ncode=Ncode, q=q, blowup=blowup,
376	                code=code)

379	def prove(com, pt, claimed, t=32):
380	    """Produce an evaluation proof that S~(pt) == claimed for the committed S."""
381	    q = com["q"]
382	    r, k, n1, Ncode = com["r"], com["k"], com["n1"], com["Ncode"]
383	    pt = [int(x) % q for x in pt]
384	    assert len(pt) == com["nb"], "point arity must match the committed table"
385	    a = [int(x) % q for x in np.asarray(eq_table(pt[:n1], q)).tolist()]
386	    M = com["M"]
387	    seed0 = _digest(com["root"], _ser(pt, q), _ser([claimed], q))
388	    rho = _challenges(seed0, b"rho", r, q)
389	    # combined messages (len k): v = a^T M (evaluation), w = rho^T M (proximity)
390	    v = [sum(a[i] * M[i][j] for i in range(r)) % q for j in range(k)]
391	    w = [sum(rho[i] * M[i][j] for i in range(r)) % q for j in range(k)]
392	    seed1 = _digest(seed0, _ser(v, q), _ser(w, q))
393	    cols = _distinct_challenges(seed1, b"col", min(t, Ncode), Ncode)
394	    opened = [(c, [com["Mhat"][i][c] for i in range(r)],
395	               _merkle_path(com["levels"], c)) for c in cols]
396	    return dict(v=v, w=w, opened=opened, r=r, k=k, n1=n1, Ncode=Ncode,
397	                nb=com["nb"], code=com["code"])

400	def verify(root, pt, claimed, proof, t=32, blowup=4, q=Q, stats=None):
401	    """Verify an evaluation proof.  Returns (ok, vops): ok is acceptance, vops is
402	    the count of field-element operations the verifier performs in its dominant
403	    loops (the SUB-sqrt-x leading term).  When stats is given, vops is added to
404	    stats['vcommit_ops'].  The full 2^nb table is never read."""
405	    code = proof.get("code", "rs")
406	    nb = len(pt)
407	    n2 = nb // 2
408	    n1 = nb - n2
409	    r, k = 1 << n1, 1 << n2
410	    Ncode = _code_ncode(code, k, q, blowup)
411	    vops = 0
412	
413	    def done(ok):
414	        if stats is not None:
415	            stats["vcommit_ops"] = stats.get("vcommit_ops", 0) + vops
416	        return ok, vops
417	
418	    # structural sanity (recomputed independently from nb + public params)
419	    if proof["r"] != r or proof["k"] != k or proof["Ncode"] != Ncode:
420	        return done(False)
421	    v = [int(x) % q for x in proof["v"]]
422	    w = [int(x) % q for x in proof["w"]]
423	    if len(v) != k or len(w) != k:
424	        return done(False)
425	    pt = [int(x) % q for x in pt]
426	    claimed = int(claimed) % q
427	    a = [int(x) % q for x in np.asarray(eq_table(pt[:n1], q)).tolist()]
428	    b = [int(x) % q for x in np.asarray(eq_table(pt[n1:], q)).tolist()]
429	
430	    # (1) evaluation binding:  <v, b> == claimed
431	    ev = sum(v[j] * b[j] for j in range(k)) % q
432	    vops += k
433	    if ev != claimed:
434	        return done(False)
435	
436	    # recompute the Fiat-Shamir challenges
437	    seed0 = _digest(root, _ser(pt, q), _ser([claimed], q))
438	    rho = _challenges(seed0, b"rho", r, q)
439	    seed1 = _digest(seed0, _ser(v, q), _ser(w, q))
440	    cols = _distinct_challenges(seed1, b"col", min(t, Ncode), Ncode)
441	    if [c for (c, _, _) in proof["opened"]] != cols:
442	        return done(False)
443	
444	    # for a linear-time code the verifier re-encodes the full combined messages
445	    # ONCE (O(N)=O(k), the linear-time encode) and indexes the queried columns;
446	    # for RS it evaluates Enc(.)[c] per column (O(k) each).  Either way O(t(r+k)).
447	    if code == "expander":
448	        pl = _exp_plan(k, q)
449	        ops_box = [0]
450	        Vcw = _exp_encode(v, q, pl, ops_box)
451	        Wcw = _exp_encode(w, q, pl, ops_box)
452	        vops += ops_box[0]
453	
454	    # (2) per-column: Merkle membership + linear-code consistency for v and w
455	    for (c, colvec, path) in proof["opened"]:
456	        if len(colvec) != r:
457	            return done(False)
458	        colvec = [int(x) % q for x in colvec]
459	        leaf = _digest(b"col", c.to_bytes(4, "big"), _ser(colvec, q))
460	        if not _merkle_check(root, c, leaf, path):
461	            return done(False)
462	        dot_a = sum(a[i] * colvec[i] for i in range(r)) % q
463	        dot_rho = sum(rho[i] * colvec[i] for i in range(r)) % q
464	        vops += 2 * r
465	        if code == "expander":
466	            enc_v_c, enc_w_c = Vcw[c], Wcw[c]
467	        else:
468	            enc_v_c, enc_w_c = _enc_point(v, c, q), _enc_point(w, c, q)
469	            vops += 2 * k
470	        if enc_v_c != dot_a or enc_w_c != dot_rho:
471	            return done(False)
472	    return done(True)

479	def _tamper_row(com, i0, rng):
480	    """Return a copy of com whose committed Mhat row i0 is corrupted to a random
481	    NON-codeword (Merkle root rebuilt to match -- a valid commitment to garbage),
482	    M left intact so prove() forms the honest v,w.  Models a prover that commits a
483	    matrix with a non-well-formed row (the proximity test must catch it)."""
484	    q, r, Ncode = com["q"], com["r"], com["Ncode"]
485	    Mhat = [list(row) for row in com["Mhat"]]
486	    Mhat[i0] = [(int(Mhat[i0][c]) + 1 + int(rng.integers(0, q - 1))) % q
487	                for c in range(Ncode)]
488	    levels = _merkle_build(_leaves_from_Mhat(Mhat, r, Ncode, q))
489	    com2 = dict(com)
490	    com2["Mhat"] = Mhat
491	    com2["levels"] = levels
492	    com2["root"] = levels[-1][0]
493	    return com2

496	def _forge_prove(com, pt, true_val, wrong_val, t=32):
497	    """A cheating opener: forge a message v' with <v',b>=wrong_val (so it passes the
498	    evaluation binding) by perturbing ONE coordinate of the honest v.  Everything
499	    else is opened honestly.  The queried-column consistency Enc(v')[c]=<a,col> must
500	    then fail (v' != a^T M)."""
501	    q = com["q"]
502	    r, k, n1, Ncode = com["r"], com["k"], com["n1"], com["Ncode"]
503	    pt = [int(x) % q for x in pt]
504	    a = [int(x) % q for x in np.asarray(eq_table(pt[:n1], q)).tolist()]
505	    b = [int(x) % q for x in np.asarray(eq_table(pt[n1:], q)).tolist()]
506	    M = com["M"]
507	    seed0 = _digest(com["root"], _ser(pt, q), _ser([wrong_val % q], q))
508	    rho = _challenges(seed0, b"rho", r, q)
509	    v = [sum(a[i] * M[i][j] for i in range(r)) % q for j in range(k)]
510	    w = [sum(rho[i] * M[i][j] for i in range(r)) % q for j in range(k)]
511	    # bend v at a coordinate with b[j0] != 0 so <v',b> = wrong_val
512	    j0 = next(j for j in range(k) if b[j] != 0)
513	    delta = (wrong_val - true_val) % q
514	    v[j0] = (v[j0] + delta * pow(b[j0], q - 2, q)) % q
515	    seed1 = _digest(seed0, _ser(v, q), _ser(w, q))
516	    cols = _distinct_challenges(seed1, b"col", min(t, Ncode), Ncode)
517	    opened = [(c, [com["Mhat"][i][c] for i in range(r)],
518	               _merkle_path(com["levels"], c)) for c in cols]
519	    return dict(v=v, w=w, opened=opened, r=r, k=k, n1=n1, Ncode=Ncode,
520	                nb=com["nb"], code=com["code"])

694	def _slope(xs, ys):
695	    k = len(xs)
696	    mx, my = sum(xs) / k, sum(ys) / k
697	    num = sum((a - mx) * (b - my) for a, b in zip(xs, ys))
698	    den = sum((a - mx) ** 2 for a in xs)
699	    return num / den if den else 0.0

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
pcs_commit.py -- S508, a hash-based multilinear polynomial commitment (tensor /
Ligero-Brakedown style) with a SUB-sqrt(x) verifier, for the chain's two
one-time S_0 base closes.

WHERE THIS SITS.  The compressed pi(x) chain (compressed_layer.run_chain) is now
per-layer LEAF-EVAL-FREE (S506 batch_ub): every per-layer carried claim threads
to the base, and the only verifier work whose cost grows with x is ONE-TIME --
the two S_0 base closes, each a DIRECT mle_eval over an O(sqrt x)=2^nb-size table
(`C == mle_eval(S0, z)` at compressed_layer.py:1047).  The whole-chain verifier
op-count (S507 `--bench-verifier-ops`) is therefore Theta(sqrt x): per-layer 0,
one-time 2*2^nb.  That one-time 2^nb term is the LAST thing between the current
state and a SUCCINCT (polylog / sub-sqrt x) verifier.

WHAT THIS BUILDS.  A polynomial commitment for a multilinear S~ over nb variables
whose EVALUATION-PROOF VERIFIER is O(sqrt(2^nb) * polylog) = O(x^{1/4} * polylog),
i.e. sub-sqrt(x).  Tensor / Ligero-Brakedown construction:

  * Reshape the 2^nb-entry table S (MSB-first) into an r x k matrix M, r=2^{n1},
    k=2^{n2}, n1+n2=nb (row bits = high n1, col bits = low n2: M = S.reshape(r,k)).
  * eq~(pt, .) factors over the bit split, eq~(pt,w)=eq~(pt_hi,w_hi)*eq~(pt_lo,w_lo),
    so with the tensor vectors a=eq_table(pt_hi) (len r), b=eq_table(pt_lo) (len k):
        S~(pt) = sum_{i,j} M[i,j] a[i] b[j] = a^T M b.
  * COMMIT: Reed-Solomon-encode each ROW of M (a degree-<k message) to a length-N
    codeword (N=blowup*k evaluation points), giving Mhat (r x N); Merkle-commit the
    N COLUMNS of Mhat (sha256, the collision-resistant-hash / random-oracle
    stand-in).  The commitment is the Merkle root.
  * OPEN (Fiat-Shamir, non-interactive): derive a proximity vector rho<-RO(root,pt,
    claimed) (len r); the prover sends the two combined MESSAGES v=a^T M (the
    evaluation combination, len k) and w=rho^T M (the proximity combination, len k),
    then opens t columns Q<-RO(root,pt,claimed,v,w) with Merkle paths.
  * VERIFY:  (1) evaluation binding  <v, b> == claimed;  (2) for each queried col c:
    the revealed column Mhat[:,c] hashes to the committed root (Merkle), AND
    Enc(v)[c] == <a, Mhat[:,c]>  AND  Enc(w)[c] == <rho, Mhat[:,c]>  (encoding is
    linear, so for an honest codeword matrix Enc(a^T M)[c] = a^T Mhat[:,c]).

  Verifier cost: reading v,w O(k); <v,b> O(k); per queried column two length-r dot
  products + two length-k encodings = O(t(r+k)) field ops + O(t r) hashed elements
  for the Merkle paths.  With r,k ~ 2^{nb/2} ~ x^{1/4} and t fixed, that is
  O(x^{1/4} * polylog) -- SUB-sqrt(x).  The full 2^nb table never touches the
  verifier; it lives only in the prover's commit/open.

SOUNDNESS (standard Ligero/Brakedown, under a collision-resistant hash / RO).
The Merkle root binds Mhat (collision resistance).  The random proximity test
(rho, t columns) forces the committed Mhat to be close to a matrix whose rows are
codewords, so it decodes to a unique M.  The evaluation columns then pin v=a^T M,
and <v,b>=claimed forces claimed = S~(pt) for that committed M.  A wrong claimed
value fails (1) outright (the honest v has <v,b>=true value); a prover who instead
forges v' with <v',b>=wrong has Enc(v') differing from a^T Mhat in >= N-(k-1)
columns (two degree-<k polys agree on < k points), caught by some queried column
with prob >= 1-((k-1)/N)^t; a tampered (non-codeword) committed row is caught by
the proximity column checks with the same bound; a tampered REVEALED column fails
its Merkle path.  This is a soundness ARGUMENT verified here empirically by the
cheating-prover tests, not a machine-checked proof.

HONEST SCOPE.  (i) The win is in the SCALING (op count slope ~0.25 in x, sub-sqrt),
NOT the absolute count at reachable n: the verifier touches ~ t*(2r+2k) ~ 4t*x^{1/4}
field elements, which only drops below the direct 2^nb close once 2^{nb/2} > ~4t,
i.e. nb > ~2*log2(4t) (~nb>=15, n>=30 at t=32) -- beyond the demo's reachable n,
exactly like the S506 wall-clock note.  The bench reports the slope to show
sub-sqrt scaling regardless of the crossover constant.  (ii) This trades
UNCONDITIONALITY for full succinctness: soundness now rests on the hash (RO/CRH),
whereas the rest of the chain verifier is unconditional and Õ(sqrt x).  (iii) RS
needs N <= q distinct points; fine at demo n, and a production system swaps in a
field-size-free linear code (Brakedown's expander code) behind the SAME
commit/open/verify interface -- the tensor reduction and the cost are unchanged.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS.  verify disagreeing with mle_eval on an honest opening;
a forged opening / wrong claimed value / tampered codeword row accepted (above the
field bound); the verifier op count not sub-sqrt-x (slope -> 0.5 not -> 0.25); or
threading it into run_chain(--commit-base) changing the chain verdict / claimed pi.

Usage:
  python3 pcs_commit.py --selftest
  python3 pcs_commit.py --bench
  python3 pcs_commit.py --bench --field big
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import time

import numpy as np

from compressed_prover_mult_trace import (DEFAULT_Q as Q, BIG_Q, SMALL_Q,
                                          FIELDS, eq_table, mle_eval)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# hashing / Merkle  (sha256 = the collision-resistant-hash / random-oracle stand-in)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def _digest(*parts):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for p in parts:
        h.update(p)
    return h.digest()


def _wid(q):
    """Fixed byte width to serialize a field element of F_q unambiguously."""
    return (int(q).bit_length() + 7) // 8 + 1


def _ser(vec, q):
    """Deterministic byte serialization of a field vector (for hashing/FS)."""
    w = _wid(q)
    return b"".join(int(int(x) % q).to_bytes(w, "big") for x in vec)


def _challenges(seed, label, n, mod):
    """n field/index challenges in [0, mod) from RO(seed || label || ctr)."""
    out = []
    i = 0
    while len(out) < n:
        d = _digest(seed, label, i.to_bytes(4, "big"))
        out.append(int.from_bytes(d, "big") % mod)
        i += 1
    return out


def _distinct_challenges(seed, label, n, mod):
    """Up to n DISTINCT indices in [0, mod) (column queries)."""
    seen, out, i = set(), [], 0
    while len(out) < n and len(seen) < mod:
        c = int.from_bytes(_digest(seed, label, i.to_bytes(4, "big")), "big") % mod
        i += 1
        if c not in seen:
            seen.add(c)
            out.append(c)
    return out


def _merkle_build(leaves):
    """Binary Merkle tree over leaf digests (padded to a power of two with a
    fixed pad leaf).  Returns the level list (levels[0]=leaves, levels[-1]=[root])."""
    n = len(leaves)
    m = 1
    while m < n:
        m <<= 1
    pad = _digest(b"pad")
    level = list(leaves) + [pad] * (m - n)
    levels = [level]
    while len(level) > 1:
        level = [_digest(level[2 * i], level[2 * i + 1])
                 for i in range(len(level) // 2)]
        levels.append(level)
    return levels


def _merkle_path(levels, idx):
    path = []
    for lvl in levels[:-1]:
        path.append(lvl[idx ^ 1])
        idx >>= 1
    return path


def _merkle_check(root, idx, leaf, path):
    h = leaf
    for sib in path:
        h = _digest(h, sib) if (idx & 1) == 0 else _digest(sib, h)
        idx >>= 1
    return h == root


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reed-Solomon encoding (the linear code; coefficient form, points 0..N-1)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def _enc_point(coeffs, x, q):
    """Evaluate sum_j coeffs[j] x^j at field point x (Horner).  This is Enc(.)[c]
    for evaluation point x = c, the verifier's per-column encoding (O(k))."""
    acc = 0
    for cj in reversed(coeffs):
        acc = (acc * x + int(cj)) % q
    return acc


def _encode_rows(M, Ncode, q):
    """Mhat[i][c] = Enc(M[i])[c], the RS codeword of every row at points 0..Ncode-1."""
    return [[_enc_point(row, c, q) for c in range(Ncode)] for row in M]


def _leaves_from_Mhat(Mhat, r, Ncode, q):
    return [_digest(b"col", c.to_bytes(4, "big"),
                    _ser([Mhat[i][c] for i in range(r)], q))
            for c in range(Ncode)]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Brakedown-style linear-time EXPANDER code (the field-size-free row code)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# WHY.  The RS row code (above) needs N = blowup*k <= q distinct evaluation
# points -- a demo constraint that caps the committable table size and forced
# the large runs onto the 61-bit BIG_Q.  Brakedown's recursive expander code is
# a LINEAR, LINEAR-TIME-ENCODABLE code with constant relative distance over ANY
# field -- no distinct-point / N<=q requirement.  It plugs in behind the SAME
# commit/prove/verify interface: only (i) how a row is encoded (commit) and (ii)
# how the combined messages v,w are re-encoded (verify) change.  The tensor
# reduction S~(pt)=a^T M b and the homomorphic column check
#     <a, Mhat[:,c]> = sum_i a[i] Enc(M[i])[c] = Enc(a^T M)[c] = Enc(v)[c]
# hold for ANY linear Enc, so the soundness argument and the O(t(r+k))=O(x^{1/4})
# verifier are unchanged; only the code (and its relative distance delta) differ.
#
# CONSTRUCTION (Spielman / Druk-Ishai recursive code, as instantiated in
# Brakedown, Golovnev-Lee-Setty-Thaler-Wahby 2021).  Systematic, recursive:
#     Enc_n(x) = x  ||  Enc_{nm}(A x)  ||  B (Enc_{nm}(A x)),   nm = ceil(n/2)
# where A (nm x n) and B (pn x ne) are SPARSE matrices over F_q and the base case
# (n <= BASE) is a dense systematic code x || R x.  A and B are COLUMN-REGULAR
# (every input coordinate is assigned to `coldeg` output rows) so EVERY input
# influences the parity -- this is what kills the weight-1 codewords a plain
# low-density generator matrix (LDGM) would have, and is the measured difference
# between rel-distance ~0.003 (row-regular, columns missed) and ~0.45 (here).
# Encode is LINEAR-TIME: each level costs O(coldeg*n) field mults and the message
# lengths shrink geometrically (sum = O(coldeg*n) = O(k) = O(x^{1/4})).
#
# The matrices are derived deterministically from a FIXED public seed + the size
# n only (column indices) and reduced mod q (values), so the prover's commit and
# the verifier's re-encode build the IDENTICAL linear map -- a fixed public code.
#
# HONEST SCOPE.  The relative distance delta is the security parameter: the
# consistency / proximity tests catch a cheating prover with prob >= 1-(1-delta)^t.
# We MEASURE delta on the demo instances (selftest asserts min low-weight-codeword
# relative weight >= 0.3; it runs ~0.42-0.65) and pick t accordingly.  Brakedown's
# *analyzed* parameters give a proven delta (~0.07) with t~148 for 100-bit
# security; the construction shape here is theirs, the constants are demo-scale and
# distance-measured rather than from the asymptotic expander bound.

_EXP_SEED = b"pcs-expander-v1"        # fixed public seed for the code's matrices
_EXP_BASE = 4                         # base-case message-length threshold
_EXP_COLDEG = 4                       # column degree of the sparse matrices A, B
_EXP_PLAN_CACHE = {}                  # (n, q) -> plan; matrices are deterministic


def _exp_val(label, i, j, q):
    """A NONZERO field element from RO(seed||label||i||j) (matrix entry)."""
    v = int.from_bytes(_digest(_EXP_SEED, label, i.to_bytes(4, "big"),
                               j.to_bytes(4, "big")), "big") % q
    return v if v != 0 else 1


def _exp_sparse_colreg(nr, nc, coldeg, q, tag):
    """A COLUMN-REGULAR sparse matrix (nr x nc): every column is placed in
    `coldeg` distinct rows with nonzero values.  Returned as row lists of
    (col, val) -- every input coordinate thus reaches >= coldeg output rows."""
    rows = [[] for _ in range(nr)]
    d = min(coldeg, nr)
    for c in range(nc):
        rs = _distinct_challenges(_EXP_SEED, tag + b":r" + c.to_bytes(4, "big"),
                                  d, nr)
        for j, ri in enumerate(rs):
            rows[ri].append((c, _exp_val(tag + b":v", ri, c * 97 + j, q)))
    return rows


def _exp_dense(nr, nc, q, tag):
    """A dense matrix (nr x nc) as row lists of (col, val) -- the base parity."""
    return [[(c, _exp_val(tag + b":v", i, c, q)) for c in range(nc)]
            for i in range(nr)]


def _exp_plan(n, q):
    """Recursive code plan for message length n over F_q.  A plan is either
    ('base', n, N, R) or ('rec', n, N, A, sub_plan, B); N is the codeword length.
    Deterministic in (n, q); cached."""
    key = (n, q)
    if key in _EXP_PLAN_CACHE:
        return _EXP_PLAN_CACHE[key]
    if n <= _EXP_BASE:
        pn = n                                   # base parity length (rate 1/2)
        R = _exp_dense(pn, n, q, b"baseR%d" % n)
        plan = ("base", n, n + pn, R)
    else:
        nm = -(-n // 2)                          # ceil(n/2)
        A = _exp_sparse_colreg(nm, n, _EXP_COLDEG, q, b"A%d" % n)
        sub = _exp_plan(nm, q)
        ne = sub[2]
        pn = -(-n // 2)                          # parity length = ceil(n/2)
        B = _exp_sparse_colreg(pn, ne, _EXP_COLDEG, q, b"B%d" % n)
        plan = ("rec", n, n + ne + pn, A, sub, B)
    _EXP_PLAN_CACHE[key] = plan
    return plan


def _exp_matvec(rows, x, q, ops=None):
    """Sparse/dense mat-vec over F_q; rows are (col, val) lists.  Counts field
    multiplies into ops[0] if given (the linear-time encode op count)."""
    out = []
    cnt = 0
    for row in rows:
        acc = 0
        for (c, v) in row:
            acc += v * x[c]
            cnt += 1
        out.append(acc % q)
    if ops is not None:
        ops[0] += cnt
    return out


def _exp_encode(msg, q, plan=None, ops=None):
    """Encode a length-n message to its length-N codeword (systematic, linear).
    O(coldeg*n) = O(n) field mults; counted into ops[0] if given."""
    n = len(msg)
    if plan is None:
        plan = _exp_plan(n, q)
    if plan[0] == "base":
        _, _, _, R = plan
        return [int(m) % q for m in msg] + _exp_matvec(R, msg, q, ops)
    _, _, _, A, sub, B = plan
    y = _exp_matvec(A, msg, q, ops)
    ye = _exp_encode(y, q, sub, ops)
    z = _exp_matvec(B, ye, q, ops)
    return [int(m) % q for m in msg] + ye + z


def _exp_min_basis_rel_weight(k, q):
    """min over basis vectors e_j of  weight(Enc(e_j)) / N  -- the quantity that
    governs the forge cheat (the forged-v difference is delta*Enc(e_{j0})).  A
    MEASURED lower bound on the code's relative distance for the soundness claim."""
    pl = _exp_plan(k, q)
    N = pl[2]
    wmin = N
    for j in range(k):
        e = [0] * k
        e[j] = 1
        cw = _exp_encode(e, q, pl)
        wmin = min(wmin, sum(1 for v in cw if v % q != 0))
    return wmin / N


def _code_ncode(code, k, q, blowup):
    """Codeword length N for the chosen row code (independent verifier recompute)."""
    if code == "rs":
        return max(blowup * k, k + 1)
    if code == "expander":
        return _exp_plan(k, q)[2]
    raise ValueError("unknown code %r" % (code,))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# the PCS:  commit / prove / verify
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def commit(S, q=Q, blowup=4, code="rs"):
    """Commit to the multilinear S~ given its 2^nb-value table S (MSB-first).
    Returns a commitment dict; the PUBLIC commitment is `com["root"]`, the rest
    is prover state used by prove().  Prover cost O(r*k*N)=O(x^{3/4}) (one-time,
    within the prover's Õ(x) budget).  `code` selects the linear row code:
    "rs" (Reed-Solomon, needs N<=q) or "expander" (Brakedown-style, field-size-
    free)."""
    S = [int(x) % q for x in np.asarray(S).ravel().tolist()]
    N0 = len(S)
    nb = N0.bit_length() - 1
    assert (1 << nb) == N0, "table size must be a power of two"
    n2 = nb // 2
    n1 = nb - n2
    r, k = 1 << n1, 1 << n2
    M = [[S[i * k + j] for j in range(k)] for i in range(r)]
    if code == "rs":
        Ncode = max(blowup * k, k + 1)      # distance N-k+1 >= 2
        assert Ncode <= q, "RS needs Ncode <= q distinct points (raise q for large nb)"
        Mhat = _encode_rows(M, Ncode, q)
    elif code == "expander":
        pl = _exp_plan(k, q)                # field-size-free; no N<=q requirement
        Ncode = pl[2]
        Mhat = [_exp_encode(row, q, pl) for row in M]
    else:
        raise ValueError("unknown code %r" % (code,))
    levels = _merkle_build(_leaves_from_Mhat(Mhat, r, Ncode, q))
    return dict(root=levels[-1][0], M=M, Mhat=Mhat, levels=levels,
                r=r, k=k, n1=n1, n2=n2, nb=nb, Ncode=Ncode, q=q, blowup=blowup,
                code=code)


def prove(com, pt, claimed, t=32):
    """Produce an evaluation proof that S~(pt) == claimed for the committed S."""
    q = com["q"]
    r, k, n1, Ncode = com["r"], com["k"], com["n1"], com["Ncode"]
    pt = [int(x) % q for x in pt]
    assert len(pt) == com["nb"], "point arity must match the committed table"
    a = [int(x) % q for x in np.asarray(eq_table(pt[:n1], q)).tolist()]
    M = com["M"]
    seed0 = _digest(com["root"], _ser(pt, q), _ser([claimed], q))
    rho = _challenges(seed0, b"rho", r, q)
    # combined messages (len k): v = a^T M (evaluation), w = rho^T M (proximity)
    v = [sum(a[i] * M[i][j] for i in range(r)) % q for j in range(k)]
    w = [sum(rho[i] * M[i][j] for i in range(r)) % q for j in range(k)]
    seed1 = _digest(seed0, _ser(v, q), _ser(w, q))
    cols = _distinct_challenges(seed1, b"col", min(t, Ncode), Ncode)
    opened = [(c, [com["Mhat"][i][c] for i in range(r)],
               _merkle_path(com["levels"], c)) for c in cols]
    return dict(v=v, w=w, opened=opened, r=r, k=k, n1=n1, Ncode=Ncode,
                nb=com["nb"], code=com["code"])


def verify(root, pt, claimed, proof, t=32, blowup=4, q=Q, stats=None):
    """Verify an evaluation proof.  Returns (ok, vops): ok is acceptance, vops is
    the count of field-element operations the verifier performs in its dominant
    loops (the SUB-sqrt-x leading term).  When stats is given, vops is added to
    stats['vcommit_ops'].  The full 2^nb table is never read."""
    code = proof.get("code", "rs")
    nb = len(pt)
    n2 = nb // 2
    n1 = nb - n2
    r, k = 1 << n1, 1 << n2
    Ncode = _code_ncode(code, k, q, blowup)
    vops = 0

    def done(ok):
        if stats is not None:
            stats["vcommit_ops"] = stats.get("vcommit_ops", 0) + vops
        return ok, vops

    # structural sanity (recomputed independently from nb + public params)
    if proof["r"] != r or proof["k"] != k or proof["Ncode"] != Ncode:
        return done(False)
    v = [int(x) % q for x in proof["v"]]
    w = [int(x) % q for x in proof["w"]]
    if len(v) != k or len(w) != k:
        return done(False)
    pt = [int(x) % q for x in pt]
    claimed = int(claimed) % q
    a = [int(x) % q for x in np.asarray(eq_table(pt[:n1], q)).tolist()]
    b = [int(x) % q for x in np.asarray(eq_table(pt[n1:], q)).tolist()]

    # (1) evaluation binding:  <v, b> == claimed
    ev = sum(v[j] * b[j] for j in range(k)) % q
    vops += k
    if ev != claimed:
        return done(False)

    # recompute the Fiat-Shamir challenges
    seed0 = _digest(root, _ser(pt, q), _ser([claimed], q))
    rho = _challenges(seed0, b"rho", r, q)
    seed1 = _digest(seed0, _ser(v, q), _ser(w, q))
    cols = _distinct_challenges(seed1, b"col", min(t, Ncode), Ncode)
    if [c for (c, _, _) in proof["opened"]] != cols:
        return done(False)

    # for a linear-time code the verifier re-encodes the full combined messages
    # ONCE (O(N)=O(k), the linear-time encode) and indexes the queried columns;
    # for RS it evaluates Enc(.)[c] per column (O(k) each).  Either way O(t(r+k)).
    if code == "expander":
        pl = _exp_plan(k, q)
        ops_box = [0]
        Vcw = _exp_encode(v, q, pl, ops_box)
        Wcw = _exp_encode(w, q, pl, ops_box)
        vops += ops_box[0]

    # (2) per-column: Merkle membership + linear-code consistency for v and w
    for (c, colvec, path) in proof["opened"]:
        if len(colvec) != r:
            return done(False)
        colvec = [int(x) % q for x in colvec]
        leaf = _digest(b"col", c.to_bytes(4, "big"), _ser(colvec, q))
        if not _merkle_check(root, c, leaf, path):
            return done(False)
        dot_a = sum(a[i] * colvec[i] for i in range(r)) % q
        dot_rho = sum(rho[i] * colvec[i] for i in range(r)) % q
        vops += 2 * r
        if code == "expander":
            enc_v_c, enc_w_c = Vcw[c], Wcw[c]
        else:
            enc_v_c, enc_w_c = _enc_point(v, c, q), _enc_point(w, c, q)
            vops += 2 * k
        if enc_v_c != dot_a or enc_w_c != dot_rho:
            return done(False)
    return done(True)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# tests
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def _tamper_row(com, i0, rng):
    """Return a copy of com whose committed Mhat row i0 is corrupted to a random
    NON-codeword (Merkle root rebuilt to match -- a valid commitment to garbage),
    M left intact so prove() forms the honest v,w.  Models a prover that commits a
    matrix with a non-well-formed row (the proximity test must catch it)."""
    q, r, Ncode = com["q"], com["r"], com["Ncode"]
    Mhat = [list(row) for row in com["Mhat"]]
    Mhat[i0] = [(int(Mhat[i0][c]) + 1 + int(rng.integers(0, q - 1))) % q
                for c in range(Ncode)]
    levels = _merkle_build(_leaves_from_Mhat(Mhat, r, Ncode, q))
    com2 = dict(com)
    com2["Mhat"] = Mhat
    com2["levels"] = levels
    com2["root"] = levels[-1][0]
    return com2


def _forge_prove(com, pt, true_val, wrong_val, t=32):
    """A cheating opener: forge a message v' with <v',b>=wrong_val (so it passes the
    evaluation binding) by perturbing ONE coordinate of the honest v.  Everything
    else is opened honestly.  The queried-column consistency Enc(v')[c]=<a,col> must
    then fail (v' != a^T M)."""
    q = com["q"]
    r, k, n1, Ncode = com["r"], com["k"], com["n1"], com["Ncode"]
    pt = [int(x) % q for x in pt]
    a = [int(x) % q for x in np.asarray(eq_table(pt[:n1], q)).tolist()]
    b = [int(x) % q for x in np.asarray(eq_table(pt[n1:], q)).tolist()]
    M = com["M"]
    seed0 = _digest(com["root"], _ser(pt, q), _ser([wrong_val % q], q))
    rho = _challenges(seed0, b"rho", r, q)
    v = [sum(a[i] * M[i][j] for i in range(r)) % q for j in range(k)]
    w = [sum(rho[i] * M[i][j] for i in range(r)) % q for j in range(k)]
    # bend v at a coordinate with b[j0] != 0 so <v',b> = wrong_val
    j0 = next(j for j in range(k) if b[j] != 0)
    delta = (wrong_val - true_val) % q
    v[j0] = (v[j0] + delta * pow(b[j0], q - 2, q)) % q
    seed1 = _digest(seed0, _ser(v, q), _ser(w, q))
    cols = _distinct_challenges(seed1, b"col", min(t, Ncode), Ncode)
    opened = [(c, [com["Mhat"][i][c] for i in range(r)],
               _merkle_path(com["levels"], c)) for c in cols]
    return dict(v=v, w=w, opened=opened, r=r, k=k, n1=n1, Ncode=Ncode,
                nb=com["nb"], code=com["code"])


def selftest():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    # 1-5. correctness + the 4 cheat classes, over q & BIG_Q & SMALL_Q, for BOTH
    #      row codes ("rs": Reed-Solomon; "expander": Brakedown-style field-size-free).
    for code in ("rs", "expander"):
        for q in (Q, BIG_Q, SMALL_Q):
            for nb in (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8):
                for _ in range(5):
                    S = np.array([int(rng.integers(0, q)) for _ in range(1 << nb)],
                                 dtype=object)
                    pt = [int(rng.integers(0, q)) for _ in range(nb)]
                    true = int(mle_eval(S, pt, q)) % q
                    com = commit(S, q, code=code)
                    pf = prove(com, pt, true)

                    # 1. honest opening verifies and AGREES with mle_eval
                    ok, vops = verify(com["root"], pt, true, pf, q=q)
                    assert ok, (code, q, nb, "honest rejected")
                    assert vops > 0

                    # 2. wrong claimed value rejected (honest prover, wrong target)
                    wrong = (true + 1) % q
                    pf_w = prove(com, pt, wrong)
                    assert not verify(com["root"], pt, wrong, pf_w, q=q)[0], \
                        (code, q, nb, "wrong claim accepted")
                    # and the honest proof checked against a wrong target rejected
                    assert not verify(com["root"], pt, wrong, pf, q=q)[0], (code, q, nb)

                    # 3. forged opening (v' bent to match a wrong value) rejected
                    if nb >= 2:
                        pf_f = _forge_prove(com, pt, true, wrong)
                        # passes the evaluation binding <v',b>=wrong by construction...
                        assert (sum(int(pf_f["v"][j]) *
                                    int(np.asarray(eq_table(pt[com["n1"]:], q))
                                        .tolist()[j]) for j in range(com["k"])) % q
                                == wrong)
                        # ...but the column-consistency checks catch it
                        assert not verify(com["root"], pt, wrong, pf_f, q=q)[0], \
                            (code, q, nb, "forged opening accepted")

                    # 4. tampered (non-codeword) committed row rejected
                    if nb >= 1:
                        ct = _tamper_row(com, int(rng.integers(0, com["r"])), rng)
                        pf_t = prove(ct, pt, true)
                        assert not verify(ct["root"], pt, true, pf_t, q=q)[0], \
                            (code, q, nb, "tampered codeword row accepted")

                    # 5. tampered REVEALED column (single entry) fails its Merkle path
                    if pf["opened"]:
                        pf_c = dict(pf)
                        op = [list(o) for o in pf["opened"]]
                        op[0][1] = list(op[0][1])
                        op[0][1][0] = (int(op[0][1][0]) + 1) % q
                        pf_c["opened"] = [tuple(o) for o in op]
                        assert not verify(com["root"], pt, true, pf_c, q=q)[0], \
                            (code, q, nb, "tampered revealed column accepted")

    # 6. stats accounting: vcommit_ops accumulates the returned vops (both codes)
    q = Q
    for code in ("rs", "expander"):
        S = np.array([int(rng.integers(0, q)) for _ in range(1 << 8)], dtype=object)
        pt = [int(rng.integers(0, q)) for _ in range(8)]
        true = int(mle_eval(S, pt, q)) % q
        com = commit(S, q, code=code)
        pf = prove(com, pt, true)
        st = {}
        ok, vops = verify(com["root"], pt, true, pf, q=q, stats=st)
        assert ok and st["vcommit_ops"] == vops, (code,)

    # 7. it really is the SAME map as the chain's pad+mle_eval base close (both codes)
    import compressed_layer as _cl
    for code in ("rs", "expander"):
        for n in (8, 10, 12):
            x = (1 << n) - 1
            nb = max(1, _cl.isqrt(x).bit_length())
            _, sm, lg = _cl.compressed_lucy(x)
            for tab in (sm[0], lg[0]):
                S = _cl.pad(tab, nb)
                pt = [int(rng.integers(0, Q)) for _ in range(nb)]
                claimed = int(mle_eval(S, pt)) % Q
                com = commit(S, Q, code=code)
                ok, _ = verify(com["root"], pt, claimed, prove(com, pt, claimed), q=Q)
                assert ok, (code, n)

    # 8. MEASURED distance of the expander code: the min basis-codeword relative
    #    weight (which governs the forge cheat) is comfortably bounded away from 0
    #    -- the field-independent (column indices) structure gives the same support
    #    over q and BIG_Q, so distance is a property of the code not the field.
    for q in (Q, BIG_Q):
        for k in (8, 16, 32, 64):
            d = _exp_min_basis_rel_weight(k, q)
            assert d >= 0.3, ("expander distance too low", q, k, d)
    # field-independence of the codeword SUPPORT (the matrices' indices are q-free)
    for k in (8, 32):
        pl_q, pl_b = _exp_plan(k, Q), _exp_plan(k, BIG_Q)
        for j in range(k):
            e = [0] * k
            e[j] = 1
            supp_q = [i for i, v in enumerate(_exp_encode(e, Q, pl_q)) if v % Q]
            supp_b = [i for i, v in enumerate(_exp_encode(e, BIG_Q, pl_b)) if v % BIG_Q]
            assert supp_q == supp_b, ("expander support field-dependent", k, j)

    # 9. THE FIELD-SIZE-FREE WIN: over a TINY prime where RS cannot commit
    #    (Ncode = max(blowup*k, k+1) > q), the expander code commits, verifies,
    #    and rejects the cheats -- removing the N<=q demo constraint that capped
    #    the committable table size and forced the large runs onto a 61-bit field.
    qt = 17
    rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
    nb = 8                                          # k=16 -> RS Ncode=64 > 17
    S = np.array([int(rng.integers(0, qt)) for _ in range(1 << nb)], dtype=object)
    pt = [int(rng.integers(0, qt)) for _ in range(nb)]
    true = int(mle_eval(S, pt, qt)) % qt
    try:
        commit(S, qt, code="rs")
        raise AssertionError("RS should refuse Ncode > q")
    except AssertionError as e:
        assert "Ncode <= q" in str(e), e
    com = commit(S, qt, code="expander")
    assert com["Ncode"] > qt                        # codeword longer than the field
    assert verify(com["root"], pt, true, prove(com, pt, true), q=qt)[0]
    wrong = (true + 1) % qt
    assert not verify(com["root"], pt, wrong, prove(com, pt, wrong), q=qt)[0]
    assert not verify(com["root"], pt, wrong,
                      _forge_prove(com, pt, true, wrong), q=qt)[0]

    print("selftest OK")


def bench(q=Q, code="rs"):
    """The headline: the evaluation-proof VERIFIER op count is SUB-sqrt(x).  We
    tabulate, vs nb, the verifier field-op count `vcommit_ops` against the direct
    mle_eval close it replaces (O(2^nb)=O(sqrt x)), and fit the leading exponent
    in n (x=2^n-1, table size 2^nb ~ sqrt x ~ x^{1/2}, so direct ~ x^{0.5}, the
    commit verifier ~ x^{0.25}).  Falsifier: commit-verify op slope -> 0.5.  The
    expander code must keep the SAME sub-sqrt slope (it just removes the N<=q
    requirement)."""
    import math
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    print(f"q = {q};  code = {code};  multilinear-eval VERIFIER op count: tensor "
          f"commitment (sub-sqrt x) vs direct mle_eval close (O(2^nb))")
    print(f"{'nb':>3} {'2^nb':>9} {'r':>5} {'k':>5} {'N':>5} {'commit_vops':>12} "
          f"{'direct_2^nb':>12} {'ratio':>7} {'proof_cols':>10}")
    rows = []
    for nb in (4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14):
        S = np.array([int(rng.integers(0, q)) for _ in range(1 << nb)], dtype=object)
        pt = [int(rng.integers(0, q)) for _ in range(nb)]
        true = int(mle_eval(S, pt, q)) % q
        com = commit(S, q, code=code)
        pf = prove(com, pt, true)
        ok, vops = verify(com["root"], pt, true, pf, q=q)
        assert ok
        direct = 1 << nb
        rows.append((nb, vops, direct))
        print(f"{nb:>3} {1 << nb:>9} {com['r']:>5} {com['k']:>5} {com['Ncode']:>5} "
              f"{vops:>12} {direct:>12} {direct / vops:>6.2f}x "
              f"{len(pf['opened']):>10}")
    pts = rows[-4:]
    ns = [p[0] for p in pts]                      # nb increments by 2 here
    sl_commit = _slope(ns, [math.log2(p[1]) for p in pts])
    sl_direct = _slope(ns, [math.log2(p[2]) for p in pts])
    print(f"\nfitted slope d log2(ops)/d nb  (last 4 pts):  commit = {sl_commit:.3f}"
          f"  direct = {sl_direct:.3f}")
    print("(direct slope -> 1.0 per nb = Theta(2^nb)=Theta(sqrt x); commit slope "
          "-> 0.5 per nb = Theta(2^{nb/2})=Theta(x^{1/4}), i.e. SUB-sqrt x.)")
    # in chain terms nb ~ n/2, so per-n exponent alpha = slope/2: direct ~0.5, commit ~0.25
    print(f"in x: alpha_commit ~ {sl_commit / 2:.3f} (target ~0.25), "
          f"alpha_direct ~ {sl_direct / 2:.3f} (~0.5).")
    assert sl_commit < 0.75, ("commit slope not sub-sqrt", sl_commit)
    assert sl_direct > 0.9, ("direct slope not ~linear", sl_direct)


def _slope(xs, ys):
    k = len(xs)
    mx, my = sum(xs) / k, sum(ys) / k
    num = sum((a - mx) * (b - my) for a, b in zip(xs, ys))
    den = sum((a - mx) ** 2 for a in xs)
    return num / den if den else 0.0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--bench", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--field", choices=list(FIELDS), default="q")
    ap.add_argument("--code", choices=("rs", "expander"), default="rs")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.bench:
        bench(FIELDS[args.field], args.code)
    else:
        selftest()

4	> length `N = blowup·k ≤ q`, a demo constraint that capped the committable table
5	> size and forced the large runs onto the 61-bit BIG_Q. `pcs_commit.py` now offers
6	> a **Brakedown-style linear-time expander code** behind the SAME

9	> slope, same 4-class cheat panel, over q & BIG_Q & SMALL_Q, and a concrete tiny-

12	
13	## What this is
14	
15	A hash-based multilinear polynomial commitment (tensor / Ligero–Brakedown
16	style) whose **evaluation-proof verifier is sub-√x** — `O(√(2^nb)·polylog) =
17	O(x^{1/4}·polylog)`. It exists to discharge the chain's **last** verifier work
18	whose cost grows with `x`: the two *one-time* `S_0` base closes in
19	`compressed_layer.run_chain`, each a direct `mle_eval` over a `2^nb = O(√x)`-size
20	table (`C == mle_eval(S0, z)`, `compressed_layer.py:1047`).
21	
22	After S506 (`batch_ub`) the per-layer verifier is leaf-eval-free; S507 measured
23	the whole-chain verifier op-count at `Θ(√x)` (per-layer 0, one-time `2·2^nb`).
24	This module collapses that one-time `2^nb` term to `O(x^{1/4})`, so the
25	**whole-chain verifier is sub-√x (succinct under a hash assumption)**.
26	
27	## Construction (tensor / Ligero–Brakedown)
28	
29	For a multilinear `S~` over `nb` vars, table `S` of `2^nb` values (MSB-first):
30	
31	- Reshape `S` into an `r×k` matrix `M` (`r=2^{n1}`, `k=2^{n2}`, `n1+n2=nb`, high
32	  bits = rows, low bits = cols → `M = S.reshape(r,k)`).
33	- `eq~(pt,w)` factors over the split, so with `a = eq_table(pt_hi)` (len `r`),
34	  `b = eq_table(pt_lo)` (len `k`):  `S~(pt) = a^T M b`.
35	- **commit**: Reed–Solomon-encode each *row* of `M` (degree-`<k` message → `N =
36	  blowup·k` evaluation points), giving `Mhat (r×N)`; Merkle-commit the `N`
37	  *columns* (sha256 = the CRH/random-oracle stand-in). Commitment = the root.
38	- **prove** (Fiat–Shamir): `rho ← RO(root,pt,claimed)` (len `r`); send the two
39	  combined messages `v = a^T M` (evaluation) and `w = rho^T M` (proximity), then
40	  open `t` columns `Q ← RO(root,pt,claimed,v,w)` with Merkle paths.
41	- **verify**: (1) evaluation binding `⟨v,b⟩ == claimed`; (2) per queried column
42	  `c`: Merkle membership of `Mhat[:,c]` to `root`, AND `Enc(v)[c] == ⟨a,Mhat[:,c]⟩`
43	  AND `Enc(w)[c] == ⟨rho,Mhat[:,c]⟩` (encoding is linear, so for an honest
44	  codeword matrix `Enc(a^T M)[c] = a^T Mhat[:,c]`).
45	
46	Verifier touches `O(k)` (read `v,w`, `⟨v,b⟩`) + per column two len-`r` dot
47	products + two len-`k` encodings = `O(t·(r+k))` field ops. With `r,k ~ 2^{nb/2} ~
48	x^{1/4}` and `t` fixed → `O(x^{1/4}·polylog)`. The full `2^nb` table never touches
49	the verifier (it lives only in the prover's commit/open).
50	
51	## Measured — `python3 pcs_commit.py --bench` (default q = 2³¹−1)
52	
53	```
54	 nb   2^nb     r     k    N  commit_vops  direct_2^nb  ratio  proof_cols
55	  4     16     4     4   16          260           16  0.06x        16
56	  6     64     8     8   32         1032           64  0.06x        32
57	  8    256    16    16   64         2064          256  0.12x        32
58	 10   1024    32    32  128         4128         1024  0.25x        32
59	 12   4096    64    64  256         8256         4096  0.50x        32
60	 14  16384   128   128  512        16512        16384  0.99x        32
61	
62	fitted slope d log2(ops)/d nb (last 4 pts):  commit = 0.500   direct = 1.000
63	in x: alpha_commit ~ 0.250 (target ~0.25),   alpha_direct ~ 0.500 (~0.5).
64	```
65	
66	**The headline is the SLOPE.** `commit_vops` grows as `Θ(2^{nb/2}) = Θ(x^{1/4})`
67	(slope 0.5 per nb = 0.25 per `n`), the direct close as `Θ(2^nb) = Θ(√x)`. Same
68	slopes over `--field big` (BIG_Q = 2⁶¹−1).
69	
70	**Honest crossover.** The *absolute* op count crosses the direct close only at
71	`nb ≈ 14` (`commit_vops 16512` vs `direct 16384`), i.e. `n ≈ 28`. Below that the
72	commit verifier does MORE work (the `t`-query constant dominates): the win is
73	asymptotic, not at reachable demo `n` — exactly the S506 wall-clock pattern. The
74	falsifiable claim is the slope (sub-√x), which holds at every measured `nb`.

76	## Soundness — cheating-prover tests (selftest, over q, BIG_Q, SMALL_Q; nb ≤ 8)
77	
78	All rejected:
79	- **wrong claimed value** — fails the evaluation binding `⟨v,b⟩ == claimed`
80	  (the honest `v` sums to the true value).
81	- **forged opening** — a `v'` bent at one coordinate so `⟨v',b⟩ = wrong` (passes
82	  binding by construction, asserted) is caught by the column-consistency checks
83	  (`Enc(v')[c] ≠ ⟨a,Mhat[:,c]⟩`; two degree-`<k` polys agree on `<k` of `N`
84	  columns, reject prob `≥ 1−((k−1)/N)^t`).
85	- **tampered (non-codeword) committed row** — Merkle root rebuilt to a valid
86	  commitment of garbage; caught by the random proximity columns.

92	## Integration — `compressed_layer.run_chain(commit_base=True)`
93	
94	The base close branches: default = direct `mle_eval` (unconditional, `O(√x)`);
95	`commit_base` = two tensor-PCS opens (verifier sub-√x, tallied in
96	`stats['vcommit_ops']`; proof comm added to `comm`). Verdict UNCHANGED — honest
97	`claimed π == sieve`, `delta_pi` and self-consistent liar rejected — over q AND
98	BIG_Q (selftest case 23, `n ≤ 12`).

100	`python3 compressed_layer.py --bench-verifier-ops` (config **(d)** added):
101	
102	```
103	config         alpha_ops   expectation
104	a no-pcs          0.961     ops~x      (per-layer leaf closes)
105	b pcs             0.998     ops~x      (Ub openings survive)
106	c pcs+bt+ub       0.500     ops~sqrt x (per-layer leaf-eval-free; one-time 2·2^nb)
107	d +commit         0.258     ops~x^1/4  (one-time base via tensor PCS)  ← SUB-√x
108	```

110	The whole-chain verifier leading term drops `Θ(x) → Θ(√x) → Θ(x^{1/4})`. `comm`
111	slope stays `~0.60` (Õ(√x)) — the commit proof adds only an `O(x^{1/4})` term.

113	## Honest scope / caveats
114	
115	- **Computational, not unconditional.** This trades the otherwise-unconditional
116	  Õ(√x) verifier for full succinctness under a collision-resistant-hash /
117	  random-oracle assumption (sha256 stand-in). The rest of the chain verifier is
118	  unconditional.
119	- **Soundness is the standard Ligero/Brakedown argument**, verified here
120	  *empirically* by the cheating-prover tests — not a machine-checked proof.
121	- **RS field-size — now removed by `code="expander"` (S514).** RS needs `N ≤ q`
122	  distinct points (fine at demo `n`, but caps the table size and forces large runs
123	  onto a 61-bit field). The field-size-free Brakedown-style expander code (S514
124	  section below) plugs in behind the SAME `commit/open/verify` interface; the
125	  tensor reduction and the `O(x^{1/4})` verifier cost are unchanged.
126	- **Leading-term metric.** `vops`/`vcommit_ops` counts the verifier's dominant
127	  field-op loops (`O(t(r+k))`); the `O(t·log N)` Merkle hashing is also sub-√x.
128	
129	## What would falsify this
130	
131	`verify` disagreeing with `mle_eval` on an honest opening; a forged opening /
132	wrong claimed value / tampered codeword row accepted above the field bound; the
133	verifier op-count slope `→ 0.5` instead of `→ 0.25` (i.e. not sub-√x); or
134	`run_chain(commit_base=True)` changing the chain verdict / `claimed π`.
135	
136	---
137	
138	## S514 — the field-size-free Brakedown-style expander row code (`code="expander"`)
139	
140	### Why
141	
142	The RS row code requires the codeword length `N = blowup·k ≤ q` (every codeword
143	symbol is a distinct field point). At demo `nb` this is fine, but it **caps the
144	committable table size** and, in `large_x_benchmark.py`, is one reason the runs
145	use the 61-bit `BIG_Q`. A production-scale commitment (`n ≳ 120`, `nb ≳ 60`) over
146	a small or fixed field needs a code whose length is independent of `q`.
147	
148	### What
149	
150	A **systematic, linear, linear-time-encodable** expander code (Spielman / Druk–
151	Ishai recursive construction, as instantiated in Brakedown, Golovnev–Lee–Setty–
152	Thaler–Wahby 2021), plugged in behind the **same** `commit/prove/verify`:
153	
154	```
155	Enc_n(x) = x  ||  Enc_{nm}(A·x)  ||  B·Enc_{nm}(A·x),   nm = ceil(n/2)
156	```
157	
158	with `A (nm×n)`, `B (pn×ne)` **column-regular** sparse matrices over `F_q`
159	(`coldeg=4` nonzeros per column) and a dense systematic base case `x || R·x` for
160	`n ≤ 4`. The matrices are derived deterministically from a fixed public seed +
161	the size `n` (column indices, `q`-free) with values reduced mod `q`, so prover
162	(commit) and verifier (re-encode) build the **identical public linear map**.
163	
164	The only code-specific code paths are **commit** (encode each row) and **verify**
165	(re-encode the combined messages `v,w` once, `O(N)=O(k)`, then index the queried
166	columns). The tensor identity `S~(pt)=a^T M b` and the homomorphic column check
167	`⟨a,Mhat[:,c]⟩ = Enc(a^T M)[c] = Enc(v)[c]` hold for **any** linear `Enc`, so the
168	soundness argument and the `O(t(r+k))=O(x^{1/4})` verifier are unchanged.
169	
170	**Column-regularity is load-bearing.** A plain low-density generator matrix (each
171	output row picks random input columns) leaves some input coordinate unused → a
172	basis codeword of weight 1 → the forge cheat at that coordinate is essentially
173	uncatchable. Making every *input column* hit `coldeg` output rows guarantees every
174	input influences the parity. Measured min basis-codeword relative weight (the
175	quantity that governs the forge cheat — the forged-`v` difference is
